parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files serve one concern, the HTTP surface for articles and their comments. The problem is that the rule for which article routes need authentication is kept in two places that must be kept in sync by hand. ArticleController defines the routes with decorators: @Controller('articles') plus @Get('feed'), @Post(), @Put(':slug'), @Delete(':slug'), @Post(':slug/comments'), @Delete(':slug/comments/:id'), @Post/@Delete(':slug/favorite'). ArticleModule.configure copies those same paths and methods as string literals in forRoutes(...) to attach AuthMiddleware. The controller also states the auth rule a third way: its @ApiBearerAuth() class decorator says every route is protected, and its "403 Forbidden" ApiResponse entries are on a set of handlers that differs from the middleware list. For example, findAll has no 403 entry, and findOne and findComments have no API annotations at all, but all of them carry the class-wide bearer-auth annotation. Handlers such as getFeed, create and favorite read @User('id') and quietly depend on the module's string list including their route. If a route is renamed in the controller, the middleware list drifts with no error. Putting the requirement on each handler (for example, with a guard decorator) would keep the rule in one place. There is also a minor issue: an unused `Request` import from 'express' in the controller.

violations.message: ArticleModule.configure copies the controller's route paths and methods as string literals in forRoutes(...) to apply AuthMiddleware. This puts the per-route auth rule in a second place, separate from the route definitions in ArticleController, and nothing stops the two from drifting apart.

The auth rule is stated three ways that don't match: class-level @ApiBearerAuth() (all routes), '403 Forbidden' ApiResponse annotations on some handlers, and the separate AuthMiddleware route list in article.module.ts. Handlers using @User('id') silently depend on that external list.
